newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to ask Egypt to let in Irish cows.
newsitem.headline: EU to ask Egypt to let in Irish cows.

text.p: European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler is to ask the Egyptian government to lift its ban on imports of live cattle from Ireland, France and Portugal, Commission spokesman Gerard Kiely said on Thursday.

The new ban, signed on Monday, is in response to an increase in mad cow disease, or Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), in Ireland in 1996. The ban, which follows one last March, also covers live cattle imports from Switzerland.
"The Commissioner will be making contact with the Egyptian authorities to reassure them and to make it clear that European beef exports are safe from mad cow disease," Kiely said.
At a news briefing on Thursday, Kiely said that the ban was unjustified in the opinion of the Commission.
"All these countries (affected by the ban) have a total depopulation policy. If a case of BSE is found then the whole herd is slaughtered," he said.
"There is no justification for the Egyptian ban," he said.
On Thursday, Egyptian port officials let Irish cattle ships dock in Alexandria and Port Said, saying they had not been notified of the ban.
